title: Brian Blade - Wikipedia
notes: Born 25 July 1970, Shreveport, Louisiana. Gospel at Zion Baptist Church, where his father Brady L. Blade Sr. was pastor; violin and the choir first, then the drums, depping for his brother Brady Blade Jr. in the church band. Studied with Dorsey Summerfield Jr. in high school; listening to Coltrane and Monk; 'increasingly influenced by the drumming styles of Elvin Jones, Art Blakey, Papa Jo Jones, and Paul Motian'. Loyola University, New Orleans, from eighteen; 1988 to 1993 played with Johnny Vidacovich, Ellis Marsalis, Steve Masakowski and others. New York in 1992, a 'first-call' drummer for Kenny Garrett, Mark Turner and Joshua Redman. The Fellowship Band from 1997 with Jon Cowherd, Chris Thomas, Myron Walden, Melvin Butler, Jeff Parker and Dave Easley; records 1998 to 2023. Wayne Shorter's quartet with Danilo Pérez and John Patitucci from 2000 until Shorter's death. Also Joshua Redman, Brad Mehldau, Christian McBride, Chick Corea, Wolfgang Muthspiel, Joni Mitchell, Herbie Hancock, Norah Jones, Marianne Faithfull, Emmylou Harris, Bob Dylan, Daniel Lanois. Mama Rosa (2009), as a singer-songwriter. Grammy with Chick Corea for Trilogy (2013). Equipment: 'vintage Gretsch, Ludwig, Sonor and Slingerland drums'; Canopus in Japan; ride cymbals by Roberto Spizzichino, vintage A Zildjians and often a 22" K Constantinople Light Ride.

title: Transcription: Brian Blade - Alabama (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer!)
notes: Kenny Garrett, Pursuance (Warner Bros.), 'Drums by Brian Blade, Transcription by Todd Bishop', 'transcription begins after 1:50', quarter at 108, 44 bars; PDF at pdxdrummer.com. Bishop: the cymbal pattern leans towards a dotted-eighth and sixteenth, triplets in the comping. Read from the engraving bar by bar; the record autocorrelates at 107 to 108 from 1:30 to 3:00.

title: Some observations on a Brian Blade performance (Todd Bishop)
notes: A concert with Darrell Grant: a 'huge range of dynamics'; 'dancing along the top of the time rather than generating it himself'; 'linear, very horn-like conception, always playing counter lines'; plays with the rhythm section and the structure more than the soloist; a 24" medium-thin K ride, 13" and 16" toms tuned medium and wide open, Gretsch hoops.

title: Elastic - Joshua Redman (joshuaredman.com)
notes: Released 9 September 2002, Warner Bros.; Redman, Sam Yahel, Brian Blade. Blade 'a first-call drummer in both jazz and pop realms'; playing together at Smalls since 1997. On Molten Soul and Jazz Crimes: 'it feels like we're playing funk and swing at the same time'; 'There's still a lot of swing in it, especially the way Brian plays drums.'

title: Brian Blade & The Fellowship Band, "Stoner Hill", Live at Chicago Music Exchange (CME Sessions)
notes: Watched as frames for his look and kit: heavy black glasses, short natural hair, a trimmed moustache and chin beard, a navy V-neck over a pale blue shirt; a dark green kit, four old cymbals, a red Persian rug.

title: Pursuance: The Music of John Coltrane - Wikipedia
notes: Kenny Garrett's seventh studio album, recorded and released 1996, Warner Bros.; Garrett, Pat Metheny, Rodney Whitaker, Brian Blade; produced by Matt Pierson. DownBeat Readers' Poll Jazz Album of the Year 1997.

title: Come Away with Me - Wikipedia
notes: Norah Jones's debut, Blue Note, February 2002. Personnel: 'Brian Blade - drums (2, 4, 6, 8-10, 12), percussion (2, 9)'; Dan Rieser drums on 1, 5, 7, 11 (Don't Know Why is 1); Kenny Wollesen on 13; Lee Alexander bass.

title: Time Out of Mind (Bob Dylan album) - Wikipedia
notes: Blade hired by Daniel Lanois; drums on Love Sick, Standing in the Doorway, Million Miles, 'Til I Fell in Love with You, Not Dark Yet and Can't Wait, each with Jim Keltner.

title: Taming the Tiger - Wikipedia
notes: Joni Mitchell, 29 September 1998, Reprise; Brian Blade, drums; Wayne Shorter, Larry Klein.

title: Wrecking Ball (Emmylou Harris album) - Wikipedia
notes: Produced by Daniel Lanois (1995). Larry Mullen Jr. drums on most tracks; 'Brian Blade - drums on 1, Indian hand drum on 5'.

title: Footprints Live! - Wikipedia
notes: Wayne Shorter, Verve, 2002: his first official live album under his own name and the first with the Footprints Quartet, Danilo Pérez, John Patitucci and Brian Blade.

title: Freedom in the Groove - Wikipedia
notes: Joshua Redman, 1996; Peter Bernstein, Peter Martin, Chris Thomas, Brian Blade - drums. AllMusic: Redman 'attempts to work himself into hip-hop and urban dance rhythms'.
